summary: 摄影师斯特里齐奇记录了墨尔本建筑和城市生活的变化。与建筑师、出版人和艺术家合作，也使他的作品从书页延伸到壁画与展览。
logic: 战后墨尔本摄影师的生涯
与艺术家、建筑师合作创作壁画和图书
教学、展览与街头摄影的再发现

paragraphs.brief: 跨越多种媒介的移民摄影师
sentences: Mark Strizic, who died in December last year, was the last of his generation.
去年十二月去世的马克·斯特里齐奇，是同代摄影师中坚持到最后的一位。
He was the last of an important group of European émigré photographers, which also included Wolfgang Sievers and Henry Talbot, who immeasurably enriched Australian photography.
有一批欧洲移民摄影师极大丰富了澳大利亚摄影，其中包括沃尔夫冈·西弗斯和亨利·塔尔博特；斯特里齐奇是这批人中最后去世的一位。
These photographers were, in their turn, part of a larger group of émigré artists, craftspeople, designers and architects who immeasurably enriched Australia as a whole.
他们又属于规模更庞大的移民艺术家、工艺师、设计师和建筑师群体，后者极大丰富了整个澳大利亚的文化。
But Strizic was a bit different.
但是Strizic有点不同

After arriving in Melbourne from Zagreb in 1950, and taking up photography in the mid-fifties, Strizic’s subsequent fifty-year career was much more complex, diverse and manifold than any of the other émigré photographers.
他于1950年从萨格勒布来到墨尔本，五十年代中期开始摄影，随后五十年的职业经历比其他移民摄影师更为复杂多样。

He not only worked in many different photographic styles, but he was also interested in new and experimental photographic techniques, as well as book design and production, architectural murals and tertiary teaching.
他不仅以许多不同的摄影风格工作，而且对新的和实验性的摄影技术，以及书籍设计和制作、建筑壁画和大学教学感兴趣。
paragraphs.gist: 来自欧洲的摄影师为澳大利亚文化带来新视野，斯特里齐奇尤其多才，五十年间从摄影实验拓展到书籍设计、建筑壁画和高等教育。

paragraphs.brief: 胶印与跨页构成的城市影集
sentences: Artistic collaboration was fundamental to Strizic’s career, and the two major groups of his photographs in the National Library of Australia come from collaborative projects.
艺术合作对Strizic的职业生涯至关重要，他在澳大利亚国家图书馆的两组照片来自合作项目。
In 1960 Strizic worked with the architectural critic, historian and lecturer David Saunders on producing a picture book about Melbourne.
1960年，Strizic与建筑评论家、历史学家和讲师David Saunders合作，制作了一本墨尔本的图片书。
Although modestly scaled, the book, Melbourne: A Portrait, is still a charming object even today.
《墨尔本肖像》篇幅虽小，时至今日仍是一本迷人的书。

Unusually for a book of the period, the entire publication is printed using the new offset printing process, rather than the photographs being printed from plates separately engraved to the letterpress text.
当时的书通常将照片另行制版，与凸版文字分别印刷，这本书却罕见地整本采用了新式胶印。
However, Strizic’s softly sunlit, cleanly composed, almost Pictorialist photographs translated well to the pages via offset.
斯特里齐奇的照片沐浴在柔和阳光中，构图简洁，几乎有画意摄影的风格，胶印很好地呈现了这种效果。

As the book’s designer, Strizic was able to freely move the rectangular photographs up and down or across the square pages so that the composition of one visually interlocked with the composition of the next, while expansive fields of blank paper, which sometimes also included floating lines of text, brought each consecutive double-page spread together into a different graphic composition visually relating to the subject matter of the photographs.
他亲自设计版面，在方形页面上自由安排长方形照片，使相邻画面的构图彼此呼应；大片留白间偶尔点缀几行文字，每一跨页各成图景，又与照片主题呼应。
paragraphs.gist: 他与建筑评论家桑德斯合作出版《墨尔本肖像》，用胶印重现柔光照片，再借跨页构图、留白与文字让相邻图像彼此呼应。

paragraphs.brief: 父亲的影响与影集的整体设计
sentences: Although modestly scaled and priced, the book didn’t lack ambition; Saunders’ text was repeated in Italian and German, envisaging a global market for images of cosmopolitan Melbourne.
这本书虽小巧又便宜，目标却并不小：桑德斯的文字还配有意大利语和德语，期待把国际化的墨尔本呈现给全球读者。
Strizic himself acknowledged that the inspiration for the book came from a book called Light and Shade, which his father, an architect, had published on his home town of Zagreb in 1955.
斯特里齐奇说，灵感来自身为建筑师的父亲1955年出版的《光与影》，那本书拍的是父亲的故乡萨格勒布。

It was clearly to this more contemplative, ambling, European style of the ‘city book’ that Strizic aspired, rather than the strident, commercial boosterism of other Australian photo books of the time, although both kinds of book cast Melbourne in a very positive light.
显然，他向往的是这种沉思漫游式的欧洲「城市影集」，而非当时澳大利亚其他影集喧闹的商业宣传，尽管两者都对墨尔本评价很高。

The Book of the Year award which Melbourne: A Portrait won in 1961 duly recognised the integrated design of the complete book package, including a bright and chirpy cover design by Leonard French, that the offset printing, carried out by Adelaide’s Griffin Press, Australia’s premier printer of the period, had allowed.
《墨尔本肖像》赢得1961年年度图书奖，肯定的是整本书浑然一体的设计，包括伦纳德·弗伦奇明快活泼的封面；当时首屈一指的阿德莱德格里芬印刷厂以胶印实现了这一效果。
paragraphs.gist: 这本面向国际读者的城市影集受父亲拍摄萨格勒布的书启发，选择沉静漫游的欧洲风格，其封面、印刷和整体设计获得年度图书奖。

paragraphs.brief: 镜头中的墨尔本从温和到压迫
sentences: An architecturally transforming Melbourne continued as one of Strizic’s main themes for the next two decades, and he developed a distinctive style, often shooting straight into the light to produce extreme contrast, with blown-out highlights silhouetting black shadows.
此后二十年，建筑不断变迁的墨尔本一直是他的主要题材；他常朝着光源拍摄，以过曝高光勾勒漆黑剪影，形成强烈反差。
The old is often juxtaposed with the new, and hot, gritty sunlight often shears across cliff-like facades.
他常将新旧并置，炽热刺目的阳光斜切过峭壁般的建筑立面。

The people of Melbourne, caught in a headlong rush hour or in exhausted repose, also feature; but Strizic’s photographs were recording the radical expansion and verticalisation of Melbourne during this period, as skyscrapers pushed upwards and car-choked roads pushed outwards, so Melbournians are often left behind or pushed out of the way, squashed down at the bottom of his shots, or squeezed in by his constricting framing.
人群匆匆赶路或疲惫歇息也进入镜头，但他更在意城市如何向上长出摩天楼、向外扩展堵车的道路，行人因此常缩在画面底端，或被紧迫的取景挤到一旁。
By the late 1970s, Strizic’s Melbourne had changed radically from his gentle 1960s vision; it had become thoroughly dystopian, an inhuman place of ugly pavements and tangled wires.
到七十年代末，他镜头中的城市已与六十年代的温和景象截然不同：丑陋的人行道和纠缠的电线使这里几乎成了冷酷的反乌托邦。

Using a process he called ‘photochrome’ he even began to print his black-and-white negatives on colour paper, as well as experimenting with duplicating them onto colour film with high-contrast lithographic film, electrifying Melbourne with intense, sometimes even psychedelic colours that gave his cityscapes a psychological, even hallucinatory, edge.
他用称为「photochrome」的工艺将黑白底片印到彩色相纸上，又尝试用高反差制版片将影像复制到彩色胶片上，使墨尔本染上浓烈乃至迷幻的色彩，城市景象也有了心理甚至幻觉般的意味。
paragraphs.gist: 随着墨尔本高楼和道路扩张，他把行人压缩在画面边缘，又用强烈逆光与迷幻色彩，把早期温和的城市肖像拍成压迫感十足的景象。

paragraphs.brief: 将电影剧照改编成平装摄影小说
sentences: In 1967 and 1968, Strizic worked on two other important projects with Sun Books, a start-up publishing company which was experimenting with different ways of taking advantage of the boom in paperback publishing that was bringing book prices down and increasing the popular market for a diverse range of formats and subjects.
1967和1968年，他与新创的太阳图书公司合作了另外两个重要项目；平装书热潮压低了书价，也为更多形式和题材打开了大众市场，该公司正尝试把握这一机会。

For one project, Strizic worked as a stills photographer on Tim Burstall’s pioneering film 2000 Weeks, and turned the stills into a complete, cheap, paperback-novel-sized, photo-roman tie-in for the film, with each page tightly packed with his photographs and dialogue from the film.
他为蒂姆·伯斯塔尔的开创性影片《两千个星期》拍剧照，再用这些照片编成廉价、平装小说大小的电影配套摄影小说，每页都排满剧照和对白。

2000 Weeks was made in a self-consciously European art-house style, and told the existential story of a young artistic man torn between his allegiance to a still provincial Australia and the lure of bigger career opportunities of Britain.
影片刻意采用欧洲艺术电影风格，讲述一位年轻艺术家在效忠尚显闭塞的澳大利亚与追求英国更广阔的事业机会之间挣扎的故事。
It bombed at the box office, so presumably Strizic’s book bombed at the bookstore as well.
影片票房惨淡，想来他的书在书店里销量也不理想。
As a filmmaker, Burstall changed tack entirely and eventually found success with cheeky sex comedies unashamedly celebrating crass Australia.
伯斯塔尔后来彻底改变创作方向，最终凭大胆戏谑、毫不掩饰地颂扬澳大利亚粗俗一面的性喜剧获得成功。
paragraphs.gist: 大众平装书兴起时，他把艺术电影《两千个星期》的剧照和对白编成廉价摄影小说；影片票房惨淡，作者推测配套读物也难畅销。

paragraphs.brief: 人物摄影的个性与书籍版面缺憾
sentences: As a photographer, Strizic worked with Sun Books again on a posh, self-consciously arty, limited-edition book called Involvement, edited by the philanthropist Andrew Grimwade.
斯特里齐奇再度与太阳图书合作，为慈善家安德鲁·格里姆韦德编辑的豪华限量本《参与》拍摄照片，这本书刻意追求艺术气派。

The idea was that Strizic would collaborate with the painter Clifton Pugh and take photographs of the same sitters Pugh had painted over the years, and painting and photograph would be shown side by side.
按设想，他要和画家克利夫顿·普格合作，拍摄普格历年画过的同一批人物，让照片与画作并排呈现。

However, the book was not designed by Strizic himself, as had been the case with Melbourne: A Portrait and 2000 Weeks, but by the designer Les Gray, who was incapable of graphically handling the juxtaposition of the tipped-in colour plates of Pugh’s paintings with Strizic’s black-and-white photographs, so each spread had an out-of-balance, cluttered feel.
前两本书由他亲自设计，《参与》却由莱斯·格雷负责；格雷没能处理好粘贴的彩色画片与黑白照片之间的搭配，使每个跨页都显得失衡凌乱。
This, combined with the book’s pretentious leather binding and grandiose text by Geoffrey Dutton, makes for a curiously unsatisfying package.
再加上故作华贵的皮面装帧和杰弗里·达顿浮夸的文字，成书效果令人颇感失望。

In his portraits, which he took in Australia, the US, the UK and Europe, Strizic answered the angular, chromatic fondue of Pugh’s paintings by developing his own extremely idiosyncratic photographic style.
在澳大利亚、美国、英国和欧洲大陆拍摄肖像时，他发展出自己鲜明独特的风格，呼应普格作品中棱角分明、色彩交融的画面。

He doubled the speed of his 35mm film with extended development, which increased the contrast and graininess of the images, and shot his sitters against dominating backgrounds, and with intruding out-of-focus foreground elements.
他延长显影时间，将35毫米胶卷的有效感光度提高一倍，使影像反差更强、颗粒更明显，又让强势的背景和介入画面的失焦前景围住人物。
This had the effect of amplifying the sitters’ personalities, who appear to be strongly asserting themselves against their environment.
这样的处理反而突出了人物个性，仿佛他们正与环境抗衡，力图展现自我。

The head of the ABC, Sir Charles Moses, is photographed through a curtain of cigar smoke, while Barry Humphries is captured amongst the eccentric antiques of his London flat, leering at us from behind his flop of hair.
澳大利亚广播公司负责人查尔斯·摩西爵士隔着雪茄烟雾入镜，巴里·汉弗莱斯则置身伦敦公寓一堆奇异古董间，从垂下的头发后咧嘴看着我们。
In 1968 this set of photographs was exhibited, as Some Australian Personalities, at the National Gallery of Victoria, in that institution’s first one-person photography show.
1968年，这组照片以《澳大利亚人物》为名在维多利亚国家美术馆展出，是该馆首场摄影个展。
paragraphs.gist: 《参与》将他与普格为同一人物创作的照片和画作并置，书籍版面虽显拥挤，他用颗粒感和环境烘托人物个性的肖像后来获得个展。

paragraphs.brief: 用摄影记录艺术与设计作品
sentences: Strizic’s involvement with other artists, architects and designers was significant on many other levels.
他与其他艺术家、建筑师和设计师的合作在许多方面都有重要意义。
In 1988 he was commissioned to comprehensively document the works of the sculptor John Davis and the furniture designer Schulim Krimper for their Australia Council-funded monographs.
1988年，他受托为雕塑家约翰·戴维斯和家具设计师舒利姆·克林珀的专著系统拍摄作品，由澳大利亚艺术委员会资助。
Strizic’s relationship with Krimper furniture went all the way back to 1959, when he first documented his work for a National Gallery of Victoria retrospective on Krimper’s work.
他早在1959年便开始为克林珀的家具拍照，当时是为维多利亚国家美术馆举办的回顾展记录作品。
Strizic was also at home with the technological avant-garde.
他对运用新技术的先锋艺术也游刃有余。
He knew the abstract artist Asher Bilu, and in 1967 made the only surviving record of Bilu’s pioneering interactive electronic artwork, Sculptron.
他结识了抽象艺术家阿舍尔·比卢，1967年为比卢开创性的互动电子作品《Sculptron》拍下唯一存世的影像。

In this photograph Strizic was able to handle with aesthetic sympathy and technical aplomb the tricky task of lighting and simultaneously exposing for the glowing oscillating patterns on the work’s eight cathode-ray tubes, as well as its Perspex flowers, chrome spheres, and electronic control box.
要让八支阴极射线管上发光振荡的图案、有机玻璃花朵、镀铬球体和电子控制盒同时得到恰当照明和曝光并不容易，他却兼顾了审美和技术。
(Jones 2011)
paragraphs.gist: 他为雕塑和家具艺术家系统记录作品，也解决了复杂的布光难题，为比卢的互动电子作品《Sculptron》留下唯一存世的影像。

paragraphs.brief: 跨媒介的巨幅摄影壁画
sentences: Strizic also had a significant career as a muralist; he built his own photographic mural processor to print architecturally scaled murals for numerous corporate headquarters and government offices, which often combined his ‘photochromes’ with his paintings.
他也是重要的壁画艺术家，曾自制摄影壁画冲印设备，为多家公司总部和政府办公室印制建筑尺度的巨幅作品，往往把自己的彩色摄影工艺与绘画结合。
In 1970 he even collaborated with the important electronic artist Stanislav Ostoja-Kotkowski on a twelve-metre long mural for the architect Gerd Block’s Ciba-Geigy building in Preston.
1970年，他甚至与重要的电子艺术家Stanislav Ostoja-Kotkowski合作，为Preston的建筑师Gerd Block的Ciba-Geigy大楼绘制了12米长的壁画。
Ostoja-Kotkowski’s colour infra-red photography was combined with Strizic’s ‘photochromes’ in a swirling abstraction of amoeboid forms and laser light refraction.
奥斯托亚-科特科夫斯基的彩色红外照片与他的彩色摄影图像结合，以旋涡般的抽象构图呈现变形虫状图案和激光折射。

Later, in the mid-1980s, he became deeply involved with the industrial ‘Superscan’ process which made large photographic prints on canvas, an analogue forerunner of today’s digitally produced giant inkjet prints.
八十年代中期，他又深入参与可在画布上制作大型照片的工业化 Superscan 工艺，它是今日巨幅数字喷墨印刷的模拟技术先驱。
(Do any of Strizic’s architectural murals still exist, I wonder, or have they, like Sculptron, also been lost?)
我不禁想，他的建筑壁画还有没有留存，还是像《Sculptron》一样也已失落？
paragraphs.gist: 他自制设备为建筑印制巨幅摄影壁画，将摄影与绘画、红外图像等结合，后来又试验在画布上制作大型照片的模拟印制工艺。

paragraphs.brief: 影像呼应博伊德的建筑主张
sentences: A final important collaboration was with the architect and cultural critic Robin Boyd.
最后一项重要合作是与建筑师和文化批评家Robin Boyd进行的。

In 1970 Strizic photographed and designed Boyd’s book Living in Australia, in which Boyd put forward his own design philosophy to counter the ugliness which both he and Strizic saw as enveloping Australia.
1970年，他为博伊德的《生活在澳大利亚》摄影并设计版面；博伊德在书中提出自己的设计理念，以抗衡二人眼中正席卷澳大利亚的丑陋环境。

Strizic’s graphically compelling photography, in which the exposed wooden beams and large picture windows of Boyd’s domestic architecture are shot in deeply penetrating diagonal focus, reinforces the larger social message of the book.
他沿深入画面的对角线把博伊德住宅中外露的木梁和大型观景窗拍得格外清晰，富有感染力的构图强化了全书更广泛的社会主张。
The book has recently been repackaged and republished with additional photography by John Gollings.
该书最近重新装帧出版，并增收了约翰·戈林斯拍摄的照片。
paragraphs.gist: 为建筑师博伊德的《生活在澳大利亚》设计并拍照时，他用沿对角线延伸的清晰构图突出梁柱和窗户，呼应书中批评建筑环境的主张。

paragraphs.brief: 旧街景之外的文化贡献
sentences: Unlike many of his fellow photographers who established their careers in the sixties, Strizic also sustained a busy career as an exhibiting artist, either solo or in collaboration, at key commercial galleries such as Gallery A, Melbourne, and Holdsworth Galleries, Sydney.
与许多同样在六十年代立足的摄影师不同，他一直活跃于商业画廊，在墨尔本的A画廊和悉尼的霍尔兹沃思画廊等处独展或与人联展。

In 1988, after a long period teaching in the new photography departments which were starting up in Melbourne art schools and technical colleges as part of the 1970s photography boom, he returned to his early negatives of Melbourne streets for an exhibition at Christine Abrahams Gallery.
七十年代摄影热潮催生了墨尔本美术院校与技术学院的摄影系；在那里长期任教后，他于1988年重拾早年的街景底片，在克里斯蒂娜·亚伯拉罕斯画廊展出。
Since then, he has gradually become most well known as a nostalgic photographer of ‘old Melbourne’, or ‘disappearing Melbourne’, or ‘marvellous Melbourne’.
自此，他逐渐因怀旧地记录「老墨尔本」「正在消逝的墨尔本」或「辉煌的墨尔本」而最为人所知。
But, seen in its entirety, his career is much more complex than that.
但是，从整体上看，他的职业生涯比这复杂得多。

Through his constant experimentation, and his long-term engagement on many different levels with many different artists and designers, he played an important, if under-the-radar, role in much that was new, innovative, and important in Australian culture.
凭借不断实验以及与众多艺术家、设计师长期而多方位的合作，他在澳大利亚文化许多重要的创新中都扮演了低调却关键的角色。
paragraphs.gist: 晚年重展旧街景让他以拍摄「消逝的墨尔本」闻名，但贯穿创作、展览和教学的实验与跨界合作，才更能说明他对澳大利亚文化的贡献。
